question: The interval from G up to D is a:
explanation: Counting G–A–B–C–D gives a 5th and the notes are seven semitones apart which is perfect.
explanationA: G up to C is a perfect 4th. D is one step higher than C.
explanationB: G–A–B–C–D covers five letter names and G up to D is seven semitones: a perfect 5th.
explanationC: G up to E is a major 6th. D is only a 5th above G.
explanationD: G up to B♭ is a minor 3rd. D is further away than that.
